theme: Graphite GPU backends and new APIs
highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 updates to Skia m152 and introduces Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn.
highlights_body: The new Graphite pipeline bindings land alongside a backend-neutral async ReadPixels API and a dedicated Vulkan.Silk.NET NuGet package. FreeType-backed font rendering arrives for Windows Nano Server, and several native memory leaks and allocation hot-paths are fixed.

bullets.detail: The bundled Skia engine advances to m152. Upstream m151 stability fixes from after the 4.151.0 branch point are also included.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: New bindings expose Skia's next-generation Graphite rendering pipeline. Consumers can create Graphite GPU contexts for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, accessing the modern lower-overhead GPU path.

bullets.lead: Backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: A new async ReadPixels API lets callers read pixel data from GPU-backed images and surfaces without blocking the render thread, working across all supported GPU backends.
A dedicated package wraps the Silk.NET Vulkan interop layer, making it straightforward to wire up Vulkan contexts without custom P/Invoke boilerplate.

bullets.lead: Native memory leaks fixed in SKRegion, SKPixmap, and SKImage
bullets.detail: Three use-after-free and memory-leak fixes land: SKRegion.SpanIterator now roots the parent SKRegion to prevent native use-after-free; SKPixmap.ExtractSubset and With* root the pixel source; SKImage.Create on raster failure correctly releases the CoTaskMem pixel buffer.

GetEncodedText avoids an intermediate string allocation on the null-terminated fast path, SKRuntimeEffectUniforms pre-sizes its lookup map to the known uniform count, SKData.SaveTo skips a double buffer copy, and HandleDictionary caches the skip-registration reflection check.

bullets.lead: FreeType font rendering on Windows Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server environments lack the GDI font stack. SkiaSharp now falls back to FreeType on Nano Server, enabling text rendering in containerised Windows workloads that was previously broken.

bullets.lead: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server test coverage added
bullets.detail: Containerised CI test legs for Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server continuously validate SkiaSharp on these production-relevant Linux and Windows container environments.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Implemented FreeType font support for Windows Nano Server, unblocking text rendering in GDI-less container environments.
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Optimised the Windows native build to initialise the MSVC environment once per build instead of per target, reducing build overhead.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Authored the Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn.
